question:
Figure 1 is the golden sample and figure 2 is the part under test. The two frames are pixel-aligned, but figure 2 was shot under noticeably different lighting, so large areas of the two images differ in brightness without anything being wrong with the part. Ignoring the lighting difference, at most one of the candidate regions below contains a real manufacturing defect. Regions are normalized [x1, y1, x2, y2] in [0, 1] (origin top-left). Which region contains a real defect?
(A) [0.5312, 0.5789, 0.6905, 0.7382]
(B) [0.0773, 0.4082, 0.2366, 0.5675]
(C) [0.5308, 0.1279, 0.6901, 0.2872]
(D) No real defect — the two frames differ only in lighting.

Answer with only the correct option letter.

To get a closer look and confirm this is indeed a defect and not just a lighting artifact, I should zoom in on this region. Let's examine the regions listed in the options to pinpoint exactly where this defect is located.

Let's check region (C) [0.5308, 0.1279, 0.6901, 0.2872] first, as it seems to cover the area where the spot is located.

<tool_call>
{"name": "crop", "arguments": {"x1": 0.5308, "y1": 0.1279, "x2": 0.6901, "y2": 0.2872, "target_image": "[img2]"}}

After cropping region (C) from [img2], I can see a clear, distinct spot that does not match the surrounding leather texture. This appears to be a manufacturing defect, such as a stain or a flaw in the material.

To be sure, I should compare this region with the corresponding region in [img1] to confirm that the difference is real and not just a lighting artifact. Let's now crop the same region from [img1].

<tool_call>
{"name": "crop", "arguments": {"x1": 0.5308, "y1": 0.1279, "x2": 0.6901, "y2": 0.2872, "target_image": "[img1]"}}

After cropping the same region from [img1], I can see that this area in [img1] shows a consistent leather texture without any defects. The region in [img2] has a明显 different feature (the spot) that is not present in [img1].

<tool_call>

Therefore, the correct answer is (C).

<answer> C </answer>
